February 17, 27.

Engineer-in-Chief & Manager,
Electricity Department,
S. M. C.

In reply to your EAM.22 of February 9, the anti-foreign
handbills found in possession of employes of the Riverside
Power Station seem to have been distributed in furtherance
of the campaign against the employment of troops for the
protection of foreigners in China and are not intended to
incite the employes in question to strike. Efforts to trace
the source of the handbills have been without avail, but
reports by agents who kept a watch in the vicinity of the
Power Station on February 13, 14 and 15 indicate that the
distribution of these leaflets has now ceased. The Bunker
Coolie, in whose locker small and large leaflets were discovered,
when interviewed by the Police, stated that he picked them up
on Tung Ting Road which is probably untrue.

(Sd.) E. I. M. Barrett.

Commissioner of Police.

CENTRAL I. O. Station.
February 16, 1927

REPORT ON Distribution of Inflammatory Handbills among
Employees of Riverside Power Station.

Made by C. D. I. Givens. Forwarded by DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INTELLIGENCE.

Sir,

The anti-foreign handbills found in possession of
employees of the Riverside Power Station, to which reference
is made in the attached letter, seem to have been distributed
in furtherance of the campaign against the employment of
troops for the protection of foreigners in China and are
not intended to excite the employees in question to strike.
Efforts to trace the source of the handbills have been
without avail, but reports by agents who kept a watch in
the vicinity of the Power Station on February 13, 14 and 15
indicate that the distribution of these leaflets has now
ceased.

Hsiung Chang Ngoh(向中玉), a No.1 Bunker Coolie,
in whose locker several small and large leaflets were dis-
covered, has been interviewed by Det. Sergt. Papp. Hsiung
states that he picked up the leaflets on Tung Ting Road,
which is probably untrue.

Hsiung Chang Ngoh(向中玉) lives at No. 983
Tung Lai Lee(東萊里) off Yungtszepoo Road.

FEBRUARY 9, 1927.

A gist of the attached pamphlet.

A declaration of the Chinese Communist Party.

Not a day passes without the Chinese Revolutionary
movement being magnified. Labourers and peasants have
joined the struggle against imperialism and against
counter-revolutionary factors.

The period between May 30 of the year before last
and January 3 this year is the aggressive period of imperialism,
especially British imperialism, but it is also the counter-
imperialistic period of the Chinese.

The "May 30" movement marks the beginning of the
Chinese Revolutionary movement, and though it was suppressed
by the joint efforts of British, French, American, Japanese
and Italian imperialists, it soon secured the sympathy of
the Kuomintang who were, however, defeated by the Allied
Forces of Fengtien and Chihli, the puppets of British and
Japanese imperialists.

Nevertheless, with the support of the masses the
Northern Expeditionary Forces of the Southern Government
succeeded in capturing, in quick succession the cities
of Changsha, Yochow, Wuchang and Hankow, a great stroke

2
to the imperialists.
The fall of Kiukiang and the "January 3" incident
in Hankow have caused such an alarm among the imperialists
that the British, American, French, and Japanese imperialists
have, at the initiation of the British imperialists, all
entered into a contract of despatching troops to Shanghai
in addition to their naval forces in China and have also
indirectly ordered their puppets, the Fentien and Chihli
cliques, to attack the Northern Expeditionary Forces and
the Kuomingchun.
The time for a death struggle against imperialism
has come. We must enlarge and consolidate our power of
organisation in order to support the Nationalist Government
against imperialists and their tools such as the militarists,
officials, compradores, land-owners and wicked gentry. Let
us shout aloud:
I. Oppose the contract entered into between 4 countries
under the leadership of the British imperialists
for the despatch of troops to China.
Down with the secret plots of imperialists.
Withdrawal of all naval and land forces in China by
the powers.
2. Consolidate the joint front of the labourers', peasants'

3

and revolutionary forces.

3. Overthrow the yoke of political and economic domination
of imperialists.

4. Disarm the Fengtien and Chihli Forces.

5. Wipe out the counter-revolutionary factors throughout the
the country.

6. Institute people's governments in villages, towns, and
capitals.

7. Long live the Chinese Revolution.

8. Long live the Chinese labourers and peasants.

____________________

Translation of the small slip.

Long live the martyrs of the Revolution!

Shih Yang, Ling Siang Ch'i, Lieu Hwa, Tao Zing Hsu -
they all sacrificed themselves for the revolution!

What shall we do? Let us carry on their work of
revolution.

H. B. WOODFORD,
SECRETARY.

The Commissioner of Police,
Central Police Station.

Dear Sir,

For your information, we forward herewith a number of
pamphlets in Chinese which were taken from one of our bunker coolies
at Riverside. As far as we can gather, they were handed to him by
some men on the street in Yangtsepoo district.

We shall be glad to have any observations you may have to
offer in connection with the above.

Yours faithfully,

MUNICIPAL ELECTRICITY DEPARTMENT.

Engineer-in-Chief & Manager.

The attached handbill was mailed to Arthur Covey the British lawyer
and sent by him to Charge Room here last night.
If it is of any interest to you and you have not already
had a copy, will you please ask one of your staff to translate same,
as the interpreter here cannot possibly do it to-day.

R. W. Tinkler
